plain: To accept as true until proven otherwise

webster.text: To take or suppose to be true or entitled to belief, without examination or positive proof, or on the strength of probability.

more.text: To venture without positive permission; as, we may presume too far.
To form confident or arrogant opinions; with on or upon, before the cause of confidence.

example.quote: If we are in a humor to presume abuses of power, it is as fair to presume them on the part of the State governments as on the part of the general government.
